description: Sigmoid neuron: ŷ = σ(wx + b), a logistic fit trained by gradient descent on the squared error, through the squashing function.

line_docs: The prediction in the proposed notation: read right to left, W×X first, then + B, then σ of that, assigned to Ŷ.
The loss: Y−Ŷ raised to the power 2 (*2 is APL's power), assigned to L.
The weight update: ∇W L is the gradient of L with respect to W; scaled by η and subtracted, the result becomes the new W.
The bias update: the same step for B.
m.purpose: Rendered from the same record as the Math face, token for token, in an APL-style array notation that reads right to left. Nothing runs it; the glyphs are placeholders until the language's semantics are settled.
m.text:
Ŷ ← σ B + W×X
L ← (Y−Ŷ)*2
W ← W − η×∇W L
B ← B − η×∇B L
m.title: The same four lines in the proposed notation

line_docs: The prediction: the line wx + b squashed by σ into (0, 1), an S-shaped curve through x.
The loss: how far the guess is from the target, squared so misses in either direction count and big misses count more.
The weight update: move w a small step (η) against its gradient, so the loss is lower next epoch.
The bias update: the same step for b.
math.purpose: The four lines are the whole computation: a prediction squashed into (0, 1) by σ, how wrong it is, and how the two parameters move to be less wrong next epoch. This is the face the other two are translations of.
math.text:
ŷ = σ(w⁢x + b)
L = (y − ŷ)²
w ← w − η⁢ ∂L/∂w
b ← b − η⁢ ∂L/∂b
math.title: The equation as written on paper

name: sigmoid

docs: The prediction: the neuron's guess for y, squashed by σ to lie between 0 and 1. The hat means an estimate of y.
The squashing function σ(t) = 1 / (1 + e^−t): any number becomes a value between 0 and 1, so the output reads as a probability. A placeholder function glyph on the M face.
The weight, the slope of the fitted line; trained, so it changes every epoch.
The input: one of the four given x values.
The bias, the intercept of the fitted line at x = 0; trained, so it changes every epoch.
The loss: how wrong the prediction is, the squared error, averaged over the four points for training.
The target: the y value the data says goes with this x.
The learning rate η (eta): how big a step gradient descent takes each epoch; here 0.1.
How much the loss changes for a small change in w; the update steps w against it.
How much the loss changes for a small change in b; the update steps b against it.
Definition: the left side is computed from the right side.
Update: the parameter takes a new value for the next epoch; assignment across time.
Subtraction; in the loss, the residual y − ŷ.
Multiplication; written by juxtaposition on the Math face, as wx.
Square: the residual squared, so under- and over-shooting count the same and big misses count more.
Open parenthesis: group the residual before squaring.
names: gradient of the loss with respect to the weight
gradient of the loss with respect to the bias
